title: Trace async input copies and the actual consumer before alleging a mutation race
applies_when: An async submit is followed by in-place tensor masking, and a candidate alleges that a delayed CPU worker will read the changed GPU input.
lesson: Inspect the real submit implementation, selected backend overrides, copy destination, task pointer and stream ordering before building a reproduction or adding a clone. Async CPU execution does not necessarily delay the read of the original tensor. In the cited KT inference path, preparation queues expert-ID copies into pinned CPU buffers before scheduling the host callback; forward_task consumes those pinned buffers. Under the same CUDA stream, later GPU masking follows that copy, so the claimed late read of original topk_ids is not established. A CPU mock that merely retains the original tensor invents a different producer. Mutation of the original IDs is real, but independently alleging alias corruption requires a supported downstream consumer and its ownership contract.
avoid_when: Not a native KT correctness result or a blanket claim that asynchronous mutation is safe. Reopen for different copy/mutation streams without a dependency, a wrapper override retaining original IDs, host writes before an async transfer completes, pinned-buffer reuse before consumption, or a demonstrated downstream consumer requiring original IDs. Verify exact installed versions and graph behavior separately; the cited source pair does not qualify every SGLang/KT combination, NPU path or CPU-only backend.

evidence.note: The caller submits before masking and passes the device's current CUDA stream. The mask really is in-place; that fact alone does not establish a delayed CPU read.

Preparation copies into pinned expert-ID buffers; the task receives their data pointers. The inspected AMX, Native, Llamafile and General inference wrappers inherit these methods without overrides. Static source mechanism, not execution evidence.
submit_with_cuda_stream uses cudaLaunchHostFunc on the supplied stream.
cudaLaunchHostFunc runs after preceding work in its stream. Independent streams without an explicit ordering dependency do not share this guarantee.
